title: Trace contaminant buildup in sealed habitats
bottleneck: In a sealed habitat, everything off-gasses: plastics, adhesives, electronics, and the crew emit hundreds of trace volatile compounds. On Earth these disperse; in a closed loop they accumulate, and some are toxic at parts-per-million levels over months. The ISS uses trace contaminant control beds needing periodic replacement from Earth resupply; catalytic oxidizers work but add power draw and can generate their own byproducts. For a multi-year Mars mission with no resupply, contaminant load and filter lifetime are unvalidated.
why_it_blocks: Air you cannot vent must be cleaned forever; a contaminant breakthrough months from Earth, with no spare filters, becomes a slow poisoning event.
current_state: The ISS trace contaminant control system handles the current load with resupplied sorbent beds; NASA is developing regenerable systems for Mars. Multi-year no-resupply operation is unproven.
